exulta.title: Exulta
exulta.aboutText: Exulta rents stretch tents for events. This is the second version of their website: a Laravel 13 back end with a React 19 front end over Inertia, and a Filament 5 admin panel the client runs themselves. It covers the full public site — product catalog, realisations, blog, FAQ and contact — plus the operational side: media library, roles, backups, cookie consent and an automated deployment pipeline.
exulta.featureCatalogText: Tents by category with detail pages, images through Spatie Media Library, and case studies under 'realisaties' showing real events.
exulta.featureAdminText: A Filament 5 panel with Shield roles, quick create, Apex charts, impersonation and a log viewer, so the client edits content without me.
exulta.featureContentText: Blog, FAQ, partners, delivery and legal pages, all translatable and served in Dutch.
exulta.featureSeoText: Server-side rendering, a generated sitemap and robots.txt, structured SEO metadata, plus an llms.txt and an AI product feed so assistants can read the catalog.
exulta.featurePerfText: Response caching and Lighthouse reports generated per page, kept in the repo so regressions show up as a diff.
exulta.featureOpsText: GitHub Actions runs tests and Pint on every push to release, backs up the database, deploys, health-checks and rolls back on failure.

vhs.title: VHS Service
vhs.alt: VHS Service website for equestrian arena construction
vhs.aboutText: VHS Service builds and renovates riding arenas in Geluwe, West Flanders, along with the levelling and groundwork that goes with them. I built their site from scratch on Next.js 16: a black-and-white, editorial design with WebGL and scroll-driven motion, served in Dutch, French and English, and tuned hard for local search.
vhs.featureMotionText: GSAP and Motion drive scroll-linked animation, with Lenis for smooth scrolling and an OGL WebGL layer for the hero.
vhs.featureI18nText: Dutch, French and English on locale-prefixed routes, with locale detection, a cookie-remembered preference and per-language metadata.
vhs.featureServicesText: Seven arena types — from ebb-and-flow beds to GEOPAT, geofibres and cofibres — each with its own page, plus levelling and groundwork sections.
vhs.featureSeoText: Generated sitemap and robots, JSON-LD for the business and its location, and canonical handling that keeps only the production host indexable.
vhs.featureFormsText: A quote form delivered through Resend, plus a cookie consent flow where analytics only load once the visitor agrees.
vhs.featureGalleryText: A realisations gallery with a coverflow showcase, carousel and keyboard-navigable lightbox for finished arenas.

scan2talk.title: Scan2Talk
scan2talk.alt: Scan2Talk check-in flow on a phone
scan2talk.aboutText: Scan2Talk is a wellbeing check-in tool for schools, live at scan2talk.be. Students scan a printed QR poster in the hallway and share how they feel in under a minute — no account, no app install. Behind it, educators get a dashboard with trends over time and can open a private chat with a student who asks for help.
scan2talk.flowStep1Text: Find a Scan2Talk poster at school and scan it with your phone. The signed link is the only way into the flow.
scan2talk.flowStep2Text: Drag the emoji barometer from 'Slecht' to 'Super', pick a theme and select the feelings that fit. Under a minute, no typing.
scan2talk.flowStep3Text: If you want, someone gets in touch — and the student decides how and when.
scan2talk.featureQrText: Physical posters encode a signed URL that never expires. The check-in flow is unreachable without a scan, so links cannot be shared or guessed.
scan2talk.featureChatText: Token-based anonymous chat sessions with a pending queue, join and close actions, presence pings and rate limiting.
scan2talk.featureDashboardText: Overview, check-ins, students and statistics screens with Chart.js graphs of class wellbeing over time.
scan2talk.featureRolesText: Educator and admin roles via Spatie Permissions, two-factor authentication, user invites, masquerade and a pruned activity log.
scan2talk.featurePwaText: Installs to the home screen and is built mobile-first — authenticated staff on a phone go straight to their dashboard.
scan2talk.featurePrivacyText: No student accounts, a dedicated privacy page, and the dashboard and check-in routes excluded from search engines.
